learningObjective: Reason about KV Cache traffic in decode-phase attention as a memory-bound problem scaling with S_kv.

canonicalClaims.claim: Decode-phase attention is memory-bound: Q is one row per head, but K and V of length S_kv per sequence must be fully read from HBM each step; per-step traffic scales linearly with S_kv, and arithmetic intensity is very low.
conditions: Standard decode without approximations; KV cache exceeds L2 capacity.
nonImplications: Does not imply prefill has the same pattern (prefill is compute-heavy).
Does not imply MQA/GQA change the bottleneck class (they reduce KV cache size but do not turn it compute-bound).

misconceptions.whyWrong: Q is tiny; K/V dominate memory traffic.

misconceptions.claim: The KV Cache fits in L2 for typical serving loads.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For long context and moderate batches, KV cache is many MB per sequence — far beyond L2.

misconceptions.claim: The hardware compresses KV Cache automatically.
misconceptions.whyWrong: No automatic compression; software-level KV quantization is required.

misconceptions.claim: Per-step decode cost is constant regardless of context length.

implementationFacts: MQA/GQA reduce KV size by K/V head sharing.
Paged KV Cache (vLLM) mitigates fragmentation but not per-token bandwidth.
